title: Kauffman and Dubrovnik polynomials from BMW algebras

items.title: Kauffman regular-isotopy and Dubrovnik conventions
items.statement:
Let
$$R_D=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1})),$$
where $z$ is not inverted. A nonempty unoriented regular link diagram is a
finite generic planar projection of one or more circles with only transverse
double crossings and an over/under marking at each crossing. Use the crossing
chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast. Its $D_0$
smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints (the through
pairing), and its $D_\infty$ smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two
bottom endpoints (the cup-cap pairing). Thus $D_0$ is the orientation-preserving
smoothing when both crossing strands point downward and the displayed crossing
has positive determinant sign. These are respectively the $A$- and
$B$-smoothings in the stated bracket chart. A positive
curl is a type-I kink whose oriented crossing has determinant sign $+1$; a
negative curl has determinant sign $-1$. The sign is unchanged if the
orientation of the whole component is reversed.

The Dubrovnik regular-isotopy evaluation $P$ is normalized by
$P(\varnothing)=1$, $P(K\sqcup\bigcirc)=dP(K)$, positive and negative curl
factors $a$ and $a^{-1}$, and
$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
Here $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ only by switching the displayed crossing. For a
nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$
and
$$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z).$$
Thus $D$ has unknot value $1$, and the universal relation defining $R_D$ is
retained even when $z$ is not invertible. These are conventions and
normalizations; ambient-isotopy invariance of $F$ is a separate theorem.

items.title: BMW coefficient extension for Dubrovnik parameters
items.statement:
Let
$$S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$$
be the universal Dubrovnik coefficient ring. Define the coefficient extension
$$T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z).$$
Inside $T$ write $z_B=q-q^{-1}$, $z_D=z_B$, $\rho=a$, and $\delta=d$. These names specify the intended BMW and Dubrovnik parameter images; the compatibility of their coefficient relations is proved separately.

items.title: Kauffman and Dubrovnik writhe-component conversion
items.statement:
For each nonempty oriented regular link diagram $K$, let $w(K)$ be its
determinant writhe and $c(K)$ its number of
components, and define $D,L,F$ by the conventions stated for this page. Then
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$
The value assigned to $L$ is independent of reversing the orientation of any
whole component. The Dubrovnik value has the stated difference-skein, curl and
circle rules; the Kauffman value has the sum-skein, curl and circle rules; and
$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z)$ is unchanged by planar isotopy and every oriented
Reidemeister move of types I, II, and III. The claim concerns these finite
diagram moves and uses the universal coefficient relations without dividing
by a skein variable.

items.title: BMW relations in the Dubrovnik parameter convention
items.statement:
Let
$$S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$$
be the Dubrovnik coefficient ring, and let
$$T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z).$$
In $T$ put $\rho=a$, $\delta=d$, and $z_B=q-q^{-1}$. Then the natural
map $S\to T$ is injective and $T$ is a free $S$-module with basis $1,q$.
Moreover, the BMW coefficient relation
$$z_B(\delta-1)=\rho-\rho^{-1}$$
holds, and the substitution $a=\rho$, $z_D=z_B$, $d=\delta$ converts
the BMW skein, curl, adjacent untwisting, and loop coefficients to the
Dubrovnik relations in the specified chart: $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$,
the curl factors are $a,a^{-1}$, and a disjoint trivial circle contributes
$d$. Here $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. No skein parameter is
divided out.

items.title: Ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra
items.statement:
Fix $n\ge0$ and a rectangle with $n$ distinct ordered endpoints on its top edge and $n$ on its bottom edge. An ordinary $(n,n)$ tangle diagram is a finite generic planar projection in the rectangle of arcs joining these endpoints and finitely many closed curves, with an over/under marking at each transverse double point and no other singularities. Two diagrams are regularly isotopic when related by planar isotopy fixing the boundary and Reidemeister moves II and III. Their regular-isotopy classes form a monoid under vertical stacking, with the $n$ straight strands as its identity. In the fixed crossing chart, $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ by switching the marked crossing, $D_0$ is the through left/right smoothing, and $D_\infty$ is the cup-cap top/bottom smoothing. The displayed $D_+$ has its over-strand running southwest to northeast; with both strands directed downward it is the determinant-positive Artin crossing. A positive curl is a type-I kink with determinant crossing sign $+1$; a negative curl has sign $-1$. Define $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ to be the $T$-algebra obtained from the monoid algebra of these classes by imposing, in every interior disk, the Dubrovnik relations
$$D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty),\qquad \text{positive curl}=a\,\text{straight strand},\qquad \text{negative curl}=a^{-1}\,\text{straight strand},$$
and the free-circle relation that adjoining one disjoint circle with no crossings with the tangle multiplies it by $d$. The symbols $a,z_D,d$ are the images from the coefficient extension. No type-I move is imposed as a regular isotopy; its effect is represented by the displayed curl relations.

items.title: The BMW presentation maps to the Dubrovnik tangle algebra
items.statement: Let $T$ be the coefficient extension and parameter substitution in the BMW-to-Dubrovnik dictionary, and let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra: its diagrams are finite generic projections of $n$ arcs with fixed ordered top and bottom endpoints and closed curves, modulo planar isotopy, Reidemeister II and III, the Dubrovnik skein relation, the two curl relations, and the free-circle relation with parameters $z_D,a,a^{-1},d$. In its fixed chart, $D_0$ is through left/right and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap top/bottom. For every $n\ge2$, send the BMW generator $g_i$ to the positive Artin crossing between strands $i,i+1$, its inverse to the negative crossing, and $e_i$ to the adjacent cup-cap tangle. This assignment extends to a unital $T$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. For $n=0,1$, define the unital $T$-algebra homomorphism by sending each scalar to that scalar times the empty or straight tangle, respectively. This claim asserts well-definedness only; it does not assert surjectivity or injectivity.

items.title: BMW tangle skein spanning by descending matchings
items.statement: For each integer $n\ge0$, let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$, with $z_D=q-q^{-1}$. Let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra formed from regular-isotopy classes with crossing rule $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$, curl factors $a,a^{-1}$, and free-circle factor $d$, where $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. Number its $2n$ boundary endpoints in cyclic order as $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. A connector is a perfect matching of these endpoints. Orient each open strand from its lower-numbered endpoint to its higher-numbered endpoint and order the open strands by their initial endpoints. Place the finitely many closed strands after the open strands in any fixed order, with a chosen orientation and initial point for each. A diagram is totally descending if, in this traversal order, the first branch encountered at each crossing is the overpassing branch. Then $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ is spanned by one loop-free, self-crossing-free totally descending tangle for each connector. These representatives can have crossings between distinct strands; their crossing data are fixed by the total traversal order. For $n=0$ the single representative is the empty tangle, and for $n=1$ it is the straight strand.

items.statement: Let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$. Put $\rho=a$ and $\delta=d$. For every $n\ge0$, the abstract presented algebra $BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)$ has a finite basis indexed by the perfect matchings of $2n$ endpoints. In particular it is spanned by $N_n$ elements, where $N_0=1$ and $N_n=(2n-1)!!$ for $n\ge1$. This is a source-module assertion about the generators-and-relations algebra, independently of any proposed map to a Dubrovnik tangle algebra.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free: transport of an explicitly indexed finite module basis along inverse coefficient-ring maps.

items.title: BMW descending matchings are independent by closure pairing
items.statement: Let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and let $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$. For each $n\ge0$, index the standard descending matching tangles by the perfect matchings $m$ of the $2n$ boundary endpoints. Reflect a second such tangle across the horizontal midline and glue corresponding boundary endpoints to obtain a closed diagram. Let $M_n$ be the matrix whose $(m,m')$ entry is the scalar Dubrovnik evaluation $P$ of this closure. Then $\det M_n$ is nonzero in $S$, its image is a non-zero-divisor in $T$, and the standard matching tangles are linearly independent over $T$. The assertion is over this universal coefficient extension and makes no independence claim after an arbitrary nonflat specialization.

items.title: BMW closure trace and stabilization scalars
items.statement:
For $n\ge1$, let $\Phi_n$ be the BMW-to-Dubrovnik tangle homomorphism over $T$, let $\widehat{t}$ denote closure of an $(n,n)$ tangle by joining corresponding top and bottom endpoints without a twist, and define
$$\tau_n(x)=d^{-n}P\!\left(\widehat{\Phi_n(x)}\right),\qquad x\in BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta).$$
Then $\tau_n$ is a cyclic $T$-linear trace, compatible with the tower inclusion $\iota_n:BMW_n\to BMW_{n+1}$ that adds one straight strand, and for every $x\in BMW_n$,
$$\tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x))=\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n)=a d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n^{-1})=a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)e_n)=d^{-1}\tau_n(x),$$
where $a=\rho$ and $d=\delta$.

items.title: BMW has the descending Kauffman tangle basis
items.statement: Over the universal coefficient extension $T$ from the BMW-to-Dubrovnik parameter dictionary, for every $n\ge0$ the natural map $\Phi_n$ from the presented BMW algebra to the Dubrovnik $(n,n)$ tangle skein algebra is an isomorphism. Both algebras are free $T$-modules on the standard totally descending, loop-free, self-crossing-free matching tangles indexed by perfect matchings of the $2n$ boundary endpoints. The common rank is $(2n-1)!!$ for $n\ge1$, with rank one at $n=0$ and $n=1$.

items.title: Compute the Kauffman polynomial from a BMW braid closure
items.statement:
**Input and output.** The input is one finite ASCII string. Its prescribed form is
`n;ell;word`, where `n` and `ell` are canonical decimal natural numbers
(`0`, or a nonzero decimal digit followed by zero or more decimal digits), and
`word` is empty if $\ell=0$ or is exactly $\ell$ comma-separated tokens of
the form `i+` or `i-`, with `i` a canonical decimal natural number. There is
no whitespace or trailing character. The output is either the rejection symbol
`REJECT` or an element of the coefficient extension $T$ with $a=\rho$ and
$d=\delta$.

1. **Parse and validate.** If the input is not in the stated syntax, if
   $\ell$ is not the number of letter tokens, if $n=0$, or if any token index
   fails $1\le i<n$, return `REJECT` and halt. Otherwise read the tokens as the
   finite signed Artin word
   $$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}, \qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\}.$$

2. **Compute the closure data.** Form the BMW product
   $b_\beta=g_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots g_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}$.
   Set $w=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\varepsilon_j$ and let $c$ be the number of cycles,
   including fixed points, of the permutation $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$ of
   $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.

3. **Enumerate a matching basis.** Work in the unit rectangle $R=[0,1]^2$ with top and
   bottom endpoints at $(j/(n+1),1)$ and $(j/(n+1),0)$, respectively, for
   $1\le j\le n$. Fix a prefix-free binary encoding of finite rational
   polygonal diagrams with over/under data, with rational coordinates written
   as reduced numerator/positive-denominator pairs. Number the tangle endpoints in cyclic order
   $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. Enumerate perfect matchings
   recursively: pair the least unmatched endpoint with each greater unmatched
   endpoint in increasing order, then continue on the remaining endpoints. For
   each matching $\mu$, scan finite diagram codes in increasing code length and
   then lexicographically. Choose the first code of a rational polygonal tangle
   diagram with that connector, no closed component and no strand self-crossing,
   in which the open strands are oriented from their lower-numbered to their
   higher-numbered endpoint, ordered by initial endpoint, and every crossing is
   over on the first traversed strand. This is the standard descending
   representative $T_\mu$. Give each polygonal segment its distinct code label
   and its orientation inherited from its strand. The spanning lemma identifies the standard descending class for each connector.

4. **Build generator matrices by skein reduction.** For every signed generator
   $g_i^{\pm1}$, form its left-multiplication matrix in the ordered basis
   $\{T_\mu\}$. The column at $T_\mu$ is computed by reducing
   $g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger endpoint
   label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order closed components by
   their least segment labels. In each closed component, start by traversing its
   least-labelled segment from its designated initial endpoint to its terminal
   endpoint; then follow the unique continuation of that component, traversing
   later segments in whichever direction reaches the next endpoint. At a crossing
   continue along the same strand, and after a smoothing continue along the
   prescribed pairing. Retain segment labels and their designated endpoints
   through switches and smoothings. This gives a deterministic traversal even
   when segment orientations do not join coherently around a closed component.
   Traverse the open strands followed by the closed components in this order,
   and select the first crossing whose first encountered branch is under. Let $R(D)$ denote the
   coordinate vector of the current tangle expression in the matching basis.
   If the selected crossing is $D_+$ in the fixed chart, put $\eta=1$; if it
   is $D_-$, put $\eta=-1$. Replace
   $$R(D)=R(D^{\mathrm{sw}})+\eta z_D\bigl(R(D_0)-R(D_\infty)\bigr),$$
   using the fixed through smoothing $D_0$ and cup-cap smoothing $D_\infty$.
   Recurse on all three resulting terms. The switched branch has one fewer
   non-descending crossing and each smoothing has one fewer crossing. At a
   descending tangle leaf, use the traversal to lift each already traversed
   segment over the remaining diagram, removing self-crossings while fixing
   the boundary; retain crossings between distinct open strands in their
   ordered layers. Remove the resulting framing curls with factors $a$ or
   $a^{-1}$ and each closed component with factor $d$. Record the remaining
   standard matching tangle and add its coefficient to that matching coordinate.

5. **Apply the matrices and evaluate the trace row.** Start with the coordinate
   vector of the identity tangle and apply the generator matrices from the
   rightmost braid letter to the leftmost, obtaining $v_\beta$, the coordinate
   vector of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$. For each matching $\mu$, close $T_\mu$ by the following fixed untwisted
   planar closure. For $1\le j\le n$ put $x_j=j/(n+1)$ and
   $\epsilon_j=1/(j+1)$, and add the rational polygonal arc

   $$C_j:(x_j,1)\to(x_j,1+\epsilon_j)\to(1+\epsilon_j,1+\epsilon_j)\to(1+\epsilon_j,-\epsilon_j)\to(x_j,-\epsilon_j)\to(x_j,0).$$

   These arcs lie outside $R$ except at their specified endpoints and are
   pairwise disjoint: if $j<k$, then $x_j<x_k$ and $\epsilon_j>\epsilon_k$,
   so their exterior lanes are nested. Orient $C_j$ from top endpoint $j$ to
   bottom endpoint $\bar j$, give its segments fresh distinct labels, and use
   this same arc system for every matching. It represents the untwisted closure
   used in the definition of $\tau_n$. Evaluate the closed diagram by the
   deterministic traversal and skein recursion of Step 4: at a descending leaf,
   straighten the traversal-ordered components, remove their framing curls with
   factors $a,a^{-1}$, remove each free circle with factor $d$, and use
   $P(\varnothing)=1$ for the empty diagram.

   Set
   $$t_\mu=d^{-n}P(\widehat{T_\mu}),\qquad \tau_n(b_\beta)=t^{\mathsf T}v_\beta.$$

6. **Return**
   $$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta).$$

items.title: The BMW Markov trace gives the Dubrovnik link invariant
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every nonempty oriented link $K\subset S^3$ and every finite signed Artin braid word $\beta$ whose oriented closure represents $K$, the corrected BMW trace value
$$Q(\beta)=-(-1)^{c(\beta)}a^{-w(\beta)}d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta),$$
where $n$ is the strand count, $c(\beta)$ is the number of closure components, and $w(\beta)$ is the determinant writhe, is independent of the braid representative. It equals the declared writhe-normalized Kauffman ambient-isotopy invariant of $K$ at $A=ia$, $Z=-iz$.

Here $\tau_n(\beta)$ denotes $\tau_n(b_\beta)$, where $b_\beta$ is obtained by replacing each letter $\sigma_i^{\pm1}$ by $g_i^{\pm1}$ in the same order.

items.title: The BMW braid-closure algorithm terminates and returns its stated value
items.statement:
For every finite ASCII input string, the BMW braid-closure algorithm parses the
form `n;ell;word`, where `n` and `ell` are canonical decimal natural numbers
(`0`, or a nonzero decimal digit followed by zero or more decimal digits), and
`word` is empty if $\ell=0$ or is exactly $\ell$ comma-separated tokens of the
form `i+` or `i-`, with `i` a canonical decimal natural number. There is no
whitespace or trailing character. It returns `REJECT` exactly when the string
fails this syntax, the parsed value of $\ell$ differs from the actual number of
letter tokens, the parsed strand count is $n=0$, or some letter index fails
$1\le i<n$. For every other input, the algorithm terminates after finitely
many basis-code searches, algebra operations, and skein reductions, and returns exactly
$$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta).$$
Here $w$ is the determinant writhe of the oriented closure, $c$ is its
component count, and $\tau_n$ is the normalized scalar closure trace. No
asymptotic complexity bound is asserted.

items.title: The Kauffman and Dubrovnik polynomials agree under the stated conversion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented link with determinant writhe $w(K)$ and component count $c(K)$, and let $Q_K$ be the value returned by the BMW braid-closure algorithm for any finite signed braid word representing $K$. Then $Q_K$ is independent of the chosen braid and
$$Q_K=F_K(ia,-iz)=-(-1)^{c(K)}a^{-w(K)}D_K(a,z),$$
equivalently,
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$
The proof covers the unknot, positive and negative curls, and both self-crossing split and mixed-crossing merge smoothing cases under the stated universal coefficient relation, without dividing by $z$.

items.title: BMW Kauffman and Dubrovnik worked cases
items.statement: For the one-component unknot, the Dubrovnik value and the normalized Kauffman value are both $1$. Adding a positive or negative curl multiplies the regular-isotopy Dubrovnik value by $a$ or $a^{-1}$, while the writhe correction leaves the ambient Kauffman value unchanged. For the two-component unlink, the Dubrovnik value is $d$, the identity $2$-braid closure has normalized trace $1$, and the BMW algorithm returns the Kauffman value $-d$. These calculations hold in the universal coefficient ring with $z(d-1)=a-a^{-1}$ and do not invert $z$.
